Part of it is that the interface between the research and the public is mediated by pop science journalism, which is motivated to make these technologies look far more monumental or controversial than they are.

This algorithm isn't "reading" your brain waves. This is part of the smoke and mirrors of the journalism. They want you to believe scientists understand how the object (or content) of thought actually relates to the neurochemical impulses in neural waves of the brain. In other words, the article would like to paint the picture that it is the "wave" that carries your thought content in some programmatic way that is readable. If you really think about the implications of this, you'll realize how absurd it is. They have no fucking idea, and it is unlikely they will for a very long time, if ever.

What is actually happening is that the algorithm is programmed to measure specific voltage changes in the language processing center of the brain that occur in correspondence with you uttering a spoken SENTENCE. There is NOTHING about individual words contained in the voltage fluctuation - it's just an ionic electrical potential.

The algorithm is mapping this particular pattern of voltage changes to the voice data recorded by the other part of the machine. In other words, it is building a lexicon. The machine equates the voltage pattern with a particular sentence. When that voltage pattern is re-created, it causes the virtual vocal tract to reproduce the sound that was recorded along with the voltage change pattern.

As you might gather, this would only work for particular sentences, you'd literally only be able to reproduce entire sentences. Why? Because the voltage changes for a single spoken word are different than for an entire sentence, and are different depending on the type of sentence and the INTENT of the speaker speaking the sentence, i.e. asking a question, making a request, expressing anger. That is, the voltage potential changes would be different for the very same sentence spoken by the same speaker, depending on their mood, their intention, who the listener was, etc. etc.

Notice in the article, they article states this was done on people who were able to speak, and they don't know how to test this yet on someone who is unable to speak!

Why? Because it likely won't work except for perhaps the most basic of phrases, and it will be devoid of much of the content we actually unpack from human speech. But, for someone who cannot speak at all, even being able to indicate something very primitive would be a cool experience. Although, it is probably still more effective for a vocoder to just read what they type.

April 25

38 Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him. - Heb 10:38 (KJV)

This scripture “the just shall live by faith” is quoting an Old Testament Scripture (Habakkuk 2:4). This Scripture was also quoted in other places in the New Testament (Romans 1:17 & Galatians 3:11). The previous verses in this chapter have been teaching that those that put faith in Jesus as their Savior, are forgiven all their sins (Hebrews 10:10, 14). It is making it clear that ALL sins are forgiven past, present and future ones. Many churches teach that you must confess all your sins to be saved, but that is not what the bible says. All our sins have been forgiven by the sacrifice of Jesus on the cross, and God does not hold our sins against us anymore (Hebrews 10:17).

God made it clear that we must have faith for Him to be pleased with us, as faith is what pleases Him (Hebrews 11:6). Our faith must be in Jesus as our Savior, and we must have faith in the Grace of God (Ephesians 2:8). God has provided for our salvation and all the Spiritual Gifts by grace, but we must do our part by putting faith in that grace. Also you must not draw back from that faith, or you become a reprobate, and you can lose your salvation (Hebrews 10:26-29). You can not do the works of the law and earn salvation by your own efforts, as it must be faith in what Christ did, and not faith in what you do (Galatians 2:16). Praise God for His abundant mercy, grace and love!

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
